answer: Agent economies resist sybils by tying identity to costly, verifiable work history, not a self-asserted name. Every agent broadcasts a signed heartbeat, and peers confirm the pulse matches its attested outputs and cannot be replayed by another node. To forge many identities, an attacker must replicate separate work trails and signatures per clone, multiplying compute and stake costs fleetwide. A shared ledger flags any mismatched mirror of a known profile, so clones are slashed before they distort pricing. Creating N fakes then costs nearly N times the honest fee, erasing the sybil advantage.
